name: What permits are needed to build a new house in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: What permits are required to build a new house in Los Angeles County, and which ones are usually missed in the early budget?
mainEntity.text: What permits are required to build a new house in Los Angeles County, and which ones are usually missed in the early budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: A new house in Los Angeles County usually requires building, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits, and many sites also need grading or other site-related approvals. Homeowners often underestimate how many separate reviews can affect the total schedule and budget. Lots with slopes, difficult access, retaining walls, or utility changes can trigger extra engineering, plan revisions, or agency coordination. The safest approach is to treat permits as a major project phase, not a line item. Ask early whether your site will need grading, soil reports, drainage design, or special fire-access requirements. Also confirm which fees are due at plan check versus permit issuance. If you are comparing builders, ask each one whether their proposal includes all permit-related soft costs or only the base construction permit. That distinction can change the real project cost significantly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most new house projects in Los Angeles County need building, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits, and some lots also need grading permits. Depending on the site and scope, additional approvals may be required for drainage, fire access, utility work, or hillside conditions. Permit fees are usually based on project valuation and scope.
